title: Real Self
definition: The organism's baseline emotional-somatic configuration that exists before cognitive identity forms — innate rhythms, sensitivities, and capacities that constitute who we are before we learned who to be.
summary: The Real Self is not a mystical concept but a biological baseline. It includes innate temperament, emotional instincts, and pre-cognitive information about safety, threat, need, and limit. It exists prior to the Role Mask and persists beneath it.

content.title: What It Is
content.content: The Real Self is the emotional-somatic configuration present at birth and early development — before cognitive identity forms. It includes: innate rhythms and sensitivities (temperament), baseline emotional capacities (curiosity, empathy, sensory truth), and pre-cognitive information processing about safety, threat, and need. The Real Self is not 'who you really are' in a mystical sense but the organism's starting configuration before adaptation shapes it.

content.title: How TEG-Blue Maps It
content.content: TEG-Blue treats the Real Self as the baseline from which the Four-Mode Gradient operates. In Connection, the Real Self has space to express. In Protection, it contracts. Under chronic threat, the Real Self becomes obscured by the Role Mask — but it doesn't disappear. Healing involves creating conditions where the Real Self can re-emerge, not constructing a new identity. What was suppressed for survival can be reclaimed when safety is restored.

content.title: Research Basis
content.content: Integrates Winnicott's True Self, Rogers' organismic self, temperament research (Chess & Thomas, Kagan), Panksepp's primary emotional systems, and Damasio's interoceptive self. Multiple traditions converge on the existence of an original, pre-adapted self that precedes social shaping. TEG-Blue grounds this convergence in nervous system biology.
